_comment: C-1 and E-0 on a leg recorded in a one-time serverless job (the Spark and Lakebase legs; design, the live-test plan): capture_job.py, the notebook, records the old client on the leg with the reference's wheels and writes the captures to the volume. Filled by `dbx_runs.py spec --template this --target serverless-env4 --notebook capture_job --sha SHA --set LEG=<leg> --set REPO_DIR=<repo snapshot> --set REFERENCE_DIR=<reference snapshot> --set CAMPAIGN=c1|e0 --set LIVE_CONFIG=<the live configuration's path on the volume> --set CAPTURE_CATALOG=... --set CAPTURE_SCHEMA=... --set TEST_DATABASE=... --set TEST_SCHEMA=... --set CAPTURE_NAMES=<a JSON object of the other placeholders' names, {} for none> --out FILE` (dbx_runs.py writes the filled spec mode 0600 and never prints it), submitted by `dbx_runs.py submit --json FILE`. Every <KEY> is filled from arguments and SDM_DBX_* environment variables; no workspace value is written here. The two Databricks legs run one after the other, never together (the one test schema holds one case's tables at a time). _timeout_seconds is each leg's job timeout, by LEG (dbx_runs.py spec sets the run's and the task's from it; the Spark leg took about 7.8 hours over 261 cases, the Spark recording's root-cause analysis of 2026-10-24); case_timeout is how long one case may run before it fails alone (capture_run.CASE_TIMEOUT).
